column1: # Re-applied on every `plan_repairs()` (see vocab/handfixes.py), so a
# re-enrichment that reintroduces the defect is corrected again rather than
# quietly winning. Every row was read by hand against the German definition
# and examples, not against the Russian gloss alone.
# article   the card is pos=noun with no article. Nominalised adjectives
#           (der/die Deutsche, das Erste) legitimately have none and are NOT
#           here — 279 of the 375 flagged were exactly that. What is here is
#           an ordinary noun that lost its article, plus pluralia tantum
# ru        the primary gloss was copied from a case twin: `das Ich` is the
#           philosophical ego, not the pronoun; `die Elf` is a football team.
# ru_all    several meanings crammed into one entry. Search scores each entry
#           whole, so "приходить, прибывать" matches the query «приходить» at
#           0.63 where the split entry matches at 1.00 — the commonest word
#           loses to any rival that happened to split its senses. Only true
#           packing is split: a Russian participial phrase ("лицо, ищущее
#           убежища") is ONE meaning and stays whole — 155 of 184 were that.

column1: # ── from the sweep of the 600 most frequent cards, 2026-07-26 ──
# 571 of 600 were correct. Of the rest, one class is new to the docs and is
# the reason these four are here: German uses the ARTICLE to separate
# homographs, and the enrichment prompt has no rule about it, so several
# genders ended up inside one card under one article. `das Band` (лента),
# `der Band` (том) and `die Band` (группа) are three different words.
# Only the meanings belonging to the card's OWN article are kept here; the
# missing genders need their own cards and are filed as A9 in info/PLANS.md.
